idiom_name: runCatching/Result and withTimeoutOrNull with an elvis substitute
implementation_notes: Kotlin folds the fallback into expressions: runCatching { primary() } returns a Result whose getOrElse/getOrDefault supplies the substitute, and in coroutines withTimeoutOrNull(200.milliseconds) turns the timeout half into a nullable value, so the degraded branch reads as plain code (fresh ?: cached). That replaces the classic degraded-mode object with a value-level decision plus one place that records the degraded state, while the structured-concurrency scope keeps the degraded branch a normal child instead of a detached task. The resilience4j-kotlin module exists for the decorator style, but the stdlib idiom covers per-call degradation without a framework.
pitfalls: withTimeoutOrNull cancels cooperatively: a blocking call (JDBC, Thread.sleep) keeps running after the timeout unless you use runInterruptible or a blocking dispatcher.
runCatching catches Throwable, including CancellationException: rethrow it or structured concurrency and job cancellation silently break.
Values returned from a timed-out block are lost, so closeable resources acquired inside need use {} or the nullable result leaks them.
